podcast.body: As a co-creator of "Blurred Lines," Pharrell Williams was successfully prosecuted alongside Robin Thicke in a high-profile copyright infringement case initiated by Marvin Gaye's estate. The court ruled that the song infringed upon Gaye's "Got to Give It Up" based on its "feel" or "vibe," resulting in a $5.3 million award to the Gaye estate. "Blurred Lines was conceived as no mage to got to give it up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Co-written with Robin Thicke, this song led to a lawsuit from Marvin Gaye's estate, accusing them of copying the "feel and sound" of Gaye's "Got to Give It Up." Williams and Thicke admitted to deliberately trying to copy the song's groove and feel as an homage. Despite expert testimony on musical differences, a jury awarded the Gaye estate over $8 million, a ruling that caused outrage in the music community and set a precedent for "feel"-based lawsuits. "the estate of Marvin Gaye objected to the sound and feel of blurred lines by Robin Thicc, a song co-written by Farrell Williams, which was released in 2013."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
